answer: Persistent reputation escrow: each agent's earned ratings are locked to its key and decay only through verified work, so a clone starts at zero while an honest agent keeps a lantern of accumulated trust. The enforcement rule requires every new key to complete a costly warm-up of auditable tasks before its ratings count, and the ledger flags any hollow cluster of fresh keys sharing behavior. An attacker must fund and operate each clone through that warm-up separately, multiplying cost per identity and defeating any atlas of cheap copies.
